assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Separate methods: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented
assertions.evidence: Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20

assertions.text: Discount ladder has multiple tiers with boundary/value sets, max 40% represented
assertions.evidence: Exactly at the cap | 40 | 40 ... Beyond the cap stays capped | {41, 45, 100} | 40

assertions.text: 30-day rolling window boundary tested at exactly 30/31 days
assertions.evidence: Exactly 30 days ago is still in window | [30/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 1 ... 31 days ago has fallen out | 0

assertions.text: 30-day window exercised at sub-day granularity, not just whole days
assertions.evidence: Rows use only whole-day offsets like 29/SINGLE, 30/SINGLE, 31/SINGLE with no hour-level distinction

assertions.text: Value sets in tier table contain exactly the values for same discount, no cross-tier contamination
assertions.evidence: Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5 ... Within second tier | {11, 12, 13, 14} | 10

assertions.text: Discount ladder table uses value sets for ticket count column to group tiers
assertions.evidence: Below first tier | {1, 2, 3, 4} | 0

assertions.text: Tier-to-discount mapping expressed once, not repeated across tables
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount table re-tests 'Adult at a tier | ADULT | 10 | 10' and 'Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40', duplicating ladder mapping already tested in discountForTripCount

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 4 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: @Description present, provides context beyond columns
assertions.evidence: "The trip ladder: every 5th single ticket in the rolling 30-day window (counting the ticket being purchased now) raises the discount by 5%, up to a 40% cap."

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Eligibility/passenger-type table includes Zone column with value set
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount table columns are 'Scenario | Traveler Category | Trips In Window | Discount?' with no Zone column

assertions.text: The rolling-window counting concern shows by row that a past purchase's zone does not affect whether it counts toward the travel count.
assertions.evidence: "Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3" and mixed-zone rows in countSingleTicketsInWindow table.

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR} in at least one row.
assertions.evidence: "Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40"

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented in the ladder table.
assertions.evidence: Table jumps from 'Exactly at second tier | 10 | 10' to 'Exactly at seventh tier | 35 | 35', omitting tiers 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%.

assertions.text: Each tier in the discount ladder is expressed as a single row with a value set.
assertions.evidence: "Exactly at first tier | 5 | 5" and "Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5" split the same tier across two rows.

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively rather than using absolute dates.
assertions.evidence: "[1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 15/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 29/SINGLE/ZONE_1]" uses days-ago values converted via @TypeConverter, no literal dates in table.

assertions.text: Multiple tables each addressing a distinct concern.
assertions.evidence: Separate @TableTest methods: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount, calculatesDiscountEndToEnd.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules.
assertions.evidence: Each table (7, 7, 5, 6 rows) targets distinct obligations without a full cross-product of unrelated dimensions.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Discount values vary across rows (0,5,10,35,40) and are not verbatim copies of input cells in every row, e.g. 'Within first tier | {6,7,8,9} | 5'.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone.
assertions.evidence: Description states "every 5th single ticket... raises the discount by 5%, up to a 40% cap" alongside explicit tier values in the table.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or fallback method name) states what the code under test does.
assertions.evidence: Method names like "discountForTripCount", "countSingleTicketsInWindow", "calculatesDiscountEndToEnd" describe system computations, not restated domain facts.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, and which the table holds constant for every row, must be visible as a column or named in the @DisplayName/@Description as deliberately held fixed.
assertions.evidence: PURCHASE_TIME is only used to construct inputs via minusDays(daysAgo); outcome depends only on relative days, and end-to-end description states 'All rows share the same purchaseTime.'

assertions.text: When a title or description quantifies over a domain, the rows must actually cover that domain.
assertions.evidence: "Zone must never affect the count." is matched by row "Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3"; "independent of travel frequency" matched by "{1, 5, 40}" value set for CHILD.
